task.description:
WF-02 Step 3 (test design) for REQ-038 on branch feature/WF02-REQ-038, commit 31599af, after REVIEWER and SECURITY-REVIEWER both PASSED (handoffs/WF02-REQ-038/step-02b-reviewer.json, step-02c-security-reviewer.json). Scope test: BACKEND-DEV's artifacts_out (apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts's redeemInviteCode/validateInviteCodeForRedemption/getInviteCodeByCode/normalizeInviteCode/parseRedeemArgs; apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's new hasPastCheckIn and registerForEvent's new internal step; apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink and the i_ StartPayload dispatch; apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts's makeRedeemCommandHandler; new i18n keys) are real behavioral surface -- real Telegram commands/deep-links writing real registrations/invite_codes/audit_log rows and sending real messages, plus a real concurrency race on invite_codes.used_count -- so the full Steps 3b/4 procedure applies, not the docs-only skip. BACKEND-DEV wrote zero new automated tests for this requirement (its own step-02 handoff explicitly names AC4's concurrency test as this step's responsibility; the only test-file change was a one-line required fixture update to registration.test.ts's baseInput for the new mandatory inviteSatisfied field) -- every case in this spec is new coverage for two test files that do not exist yet, following the same convention docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-035.md established (TEST-DESIGNER writes the full runnable source in the markdown; TEST-RUNNER creates and commits the actual files at Step 4, decisions/0006). Read GitHub issue #70 directly for the exact wording of all 11 acceptance criteria (not a paraphrase) and mapped every one to a concrete case: File 1 (apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCodeRedeem.db.test.ts, domain-layer, calling redeemInviteCode/registerForEvent/hasPastCheckIn directly) covers AC2 (personal code issued to user A refused when redeemed by user B, with A's own successful redemption as a positive control proving the refusal is identity-specific), AC3 (four sub-cases: expired, spent, unknown code string, wrong-event, each its own refusal kind, none touching registrations or used_count), AC4 (the hardest -- two genuine-concurrency cases mirroring registrationApproval.db.test.ts's already-validated REQ-035 AC5 pattern, detailed below), AC5 (requires_invite AND requires_approval -> 'requested', visible via listPendingRequestsForOrganizer), AC6 (requires_invite at full capacity -> 'waitlisted', capacity filled via a first legitimate code redemption so the capacity mechanism itself is exercised, not synthetically inserted), AC7 (two DB cases -- past-check-in admits without a code via registerForEvent directly with checked_in_at set on a prior registration, no-past-check-in refuses with 'requires-invite' -- plus one static case grepping schema.ts for any stored returning/eligibility column), AC8 (two static cases -- the design artefact's own text asserted to contain its stated FR-4 resolution and 'no column added' conclusion, plus a grep of schema.ts's own events table block for an eligibility/returning column), AC10 (the same static wishlist grep shape registrationApproval.db.test.ts's own REQ-035 AC3 case established, re-applied here), and AC11 (exactly one audit_log row on a successful redemption with the payload's inviteCodeId checked, zero rows on a refusal). File 2 (apps/bot/src/handlers/redeem.db.test.ts, handler-layer, real grammY Bot/bot.handleUpdate dispatch mirroring handlers/start.test.ts's and handlers/organizerRequests.db.test.ts's own infrastructure) covers AC1 (both entry points -- /start i_<code> and typed /redeem <event_id> <code> -- each independently dispatched against an already-consented user, each asserted to admit, set invite_code_id, and increment used_count by exactly one) and AC9 (two sub-cases: an unconsented redeemer's /start i_<code> shows the consent prompt with zero rows written anywhere, then tapping consent:agree resumes and completes the redemption; and a redeemer who never taps consent:agree stays at zero profiles/registrations rows and unchanged used_count indefinitely -- explicitly noted as this codebase's exact operational meaning of 'declining', since domain/consent.ts and handlers/start.ts were grepped and confirmed to have no separate decline affordance, only consent:agree).

AC4's concurrency-test design, given special attention per this step's task instructions: it deliberately mirrors registrationApproval.db.test.ts's REQ-035 AC5 pattern -- the SAME two-failure-mode analysis (client-side serialization masquerading as a DB-level proof; a lock scope too narrow to be the actual thing raced) and the SAME two-case structure (the requirement's literal 20-iteration/2-concurrent-caller shape, plus a higher-fan-in 10-concurrent-caller/5-iteration variant using a dedicated, generously-sized pg.Pool with an explicit pool.totalCount assertion taken immediately after firing the batch but before awaiting it, proving genuinely separate physical connections opened rather than one connection serializing statements). The load-bearing difference from REQ-035 is stated explicitly in the spec: REQ-035's race is over the events row's capacity/admittedCount; REQ-038's AC4 race is over a DIFFERENT resource, the invite_codes row's own used_count counter -- verified by SECURITY-REVIEWER's own independent trace in step-02c-security-reviewer.json (finding 2) that redeemInviteCode's load-bearing lock is `SELECT ... FROM invite_codes ... FOR UPDATE` taken fresh inside the same transaction as the uses-remain check, the registration write, and the increment, never reusing the unlocked step-2 precheck. Every seeded event in the AC4 describe block is given capacity well above the tested fan-in specifically so a false pass from capacity accidentally serializing the outcome is structurally impossible -- only the code's own row lock can be what produces exactly one winner.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-038's 11 acceptance criteria (issue #70) has at least one verification case that would fail if violated.
Each case names the exact function/handler/route exercised and the exact expected result -- no case relies on judgment.

AC4's concurrency case is genuinely probative against real concurrent Postgres access, not a sequential or client-serialized approximation, and its relationship to REQ-035's already-validated AC5 pattern is stated explicitly, including what is different (the resource being raced).
A claimed, collision-free tg_id range is stated for each new file.

result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-038.md containing: (1) the AC-to-case map covering all 11 ACs; (2) a dedicated 'AC4 -- special design note' explaining why this mirrors REQ-035's AC5 concurrency test (same two failure modes, same Promise.all-before-await + dedicated-pool/pool.totalCount evidence technique) and what is different (the raced resource is invite_codes.used_count via redeemInviteCode's own FOR UPDATE lock on that row, not the events row's capacity, independently confirmed against SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-02c trace, finding 2); (3) the full runnable source of two new test files -- apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCodeRedeem.db.test.ts (tg_id range 1_050_000_000+) covering AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6/AC7/AC8/AC10/AC11, and apps/bot/src/handlers/redeem.db.test.ts (tg_id range 1_051_000_000+) covering AC1/AC9 -- both confirmed collision-free against every existing nextTgId/tgSeq band via `grep -rn "let nextTgId\|let tgSeq" apps/bot/src` (highest existing band: inviteCodes.db.test.ts's 1_040_000_000+; both new ranges sit 10,000,000+ above it, comfortably clear of that file's own increment count).

Every function/type name, signature, and i18n catalog key referenced in the test source was independently confirmed against the actual committed files, not the design doc's prose or BACKEND-DEV's/REVIEWER's/SECURITY-REVIEWER's summaries: read domain/inviteCode.ts's redeemInviteCode (lines 616-826) and validateInviteCodeForRedemption (572-594) in full to confirm the exact step order (unlocked precheck -> lock events -> lock invite_codes fresh -> validate -> decide -> write) and the exact InviteRedemptionOutcome union members (invite-code-not-found/expired/spent/wrong-event/not-yours); read domain/registration.ts's hasPastCheckIn (132-139, confirmed it takes no evaluationTime parameter and inspects only checked_in_at IS NOT NULL) and registerForEvent's new internal step (206-218, confirmed external signature genuinely unchanged); read handlers/registration.ts's makeRedeemCommandHandler (140-207, confirmed the consent-gate-before-lookup ordering and the exact with-suffix i_<code>__<eventId> payload grammar it builds) and handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink (195-240) and makeStartHandler's payload.kind==='invite' branch (497-511, confirmed it runs before any chapter/profile concern, simplifying every AC1/AC9 fixture to need no chapter seeding) and makeConsentCallbackHandler's new invite sibling branch (707-721); read domain/event.ts's parseStartPayload i_ grammar (479-524); read i18n/en.ts's actual registration.* catalog keys (204-215) to confirm every new key referenced in the design actually exists as written; grepped domain/consent.ts and handlers/start.ts for 'decline' and confirmed no separate decline affordance exists anywhere in this codebase's consent flow (only consent:agree) -- documented explicitly in File 2's AC9 second case so TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and TEST-RUNNER don't mistake the absence of a decline button for a gap; read domain/schema.ts's inviteCodes/registrations/profiles/auditLog table definitions directly for every field name used (usedCount, maxUses, issuedToUserId, inviteCodeId, actorUserId, etc.); read registrationApproval.db.test.ts (REQ-035's own domain-layer suite) in full as the concurrency-test and audit-count-assertion precedent, and start.test.ts / organizerRequests.db.test.ts in full for the exact makeTestBot/commandUpdate/consentAgreeCallbackUpdate dispatch conventions reused here; confirmed listPendingRequestsForOrganizer's real 4-argument signature (db, eventId, lang, evaluationTime) by reading it directly rather than assuming REQ-035's own spec-file excerpt (which omitted the 4th argument in one call site) was current.

Both new files' schema imports were checked against their own bodies for unused-import lint risk and trimmed (an initially-included, unused 'users' import was removed from File 1). Confirmed no schema/migration change exists on this branch (git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts and -- apps/bot/drizzle both empty, independently re-confirmed, matching REVIEWER's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's own findings) so no new migration step is needed for either test file. Did not run any test myself -- TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 scope, per this role's 'design verification, don't execute it' boundary -- and did not modify any src/ or apps/bot/src/*.ts file.
